title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management
abstract: arXiv:2610.28708v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large retail chains must tailor assortment and pricing decisions to local customer preferences, yet even retailers with extensive sales records often have limited data for estimating demand at the store or local market level, particularly in product categories with short selling windows. Local estimation (fitting a demand model for each store on its own) can therefore be unreliable, while pooling data across stores improves estimation precision at the cost of ignoring local demand heterogeneity. We study how retailers can balance these competing effects through transfer learning under a multinomial logit (MNL) demand model. We propose a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific demand estimates with information pooled from other stores. translated_abstract: 大型零售连锁企业必须根据当地顾客偏好来调整品类和定价决策，然而即使是拥有大量销售记录的零售商，在估计门店或本地市场层面的需求时，数据往往有限，尤其是在销售周期较短的产品类别中。因此，本地估计（为每个门店单独拟合需求模型）可能不可靠，而跨门店汇集数据虽能提高估计精度，却以忽略本地需求异质性为代价。我们研究了零售商如何在多项Logit（MNL）需求模型下通过迁移学习来平衡这两种相互冲突的效应。我们提出了一种收缩估计量，将门店特定的需求估计与从其他门店汇集的信息相结合。与运营管理领域现有信息传递理论文献所基于的线性或二次设定不同，非线性MNL似然函数无法直接……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种面向MNL需求模型的收缩估计量，通过迁移学习在门店本地需求估计与跨门店信息共享之间取得平衡，从而在本地数据有限的情况下提升零售收益管理中品类与定价决策的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a shrinkage estimator for the MNL demand model that leverages transfer learning to balance store-specific demand estimation with information pooled across stores, improving assortment and pricing decisions in revenue management when local data is limited.
